summary: Round-10 minor 1 is WITHDRAWN: I measured format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentCommit.java:25 as `record SegmentCommit(String segmentKey, List<RunCommit> runs)` -- no podId in the delta at all -- so the author and the production reviewer are right and I was wrong. Keeping BOTH the data requirement and the per-segment assertion is correct. Round-10 minors 2 and 3 are verified fixed: the grep blind spot at Sequencer.java:48-50 is real (the sentence says 'The pair', so `git grep 'podId, flushSeq'` misses it, confirmed), and the new-version requirement does close the always-emit-the-new-shape mutation. Every other test-facing claim in the ADR and the notes was checked against the tree and holds: GoldenChainEntryTest's 'Do NOT regenerate' plus its byte-identical assertions, chain-delta-batched-v1.bin holding bins/a.seg with no pod, CheckpointTest's isLessThan(64*1024) at 1,600 streams, CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest's bytes[7]=1, Checkpoint.decode's strict `version != VERSION`, IngestCommitPathTest's Recording sequencer, the M3.0 segment-v0.bin quote, and every one of the eleven grep sites at the exact line numbers named. Two findings remain, both the same shape the earlier rounds kept producing: a prescription that admits the mutation it names.

findings.title: Criterion 6's 'answer a replay' obligation became vacuously satisfiable in the same commit that amended it -- detect-and-always-refuse passes
findings.failure_scenario: The pre-change criterion was unconditional: 'assigns no new offsets AND returns the original assignment'. As amended it reads 'returns the original assignment WHEN the recorded pointer names a delta carrying that triple, refusing otherwise'. The antecedent is entirely under the implementation's control. M4.10d implements detection from `lastAppliedFlushSeq`, adds the pointer FIELD that criterion 9 and ADR-0036 require, never populates it (sentinel/zero), and refuses every replay with a distinguishable error. Criterion 6 as written: 'assigns no new offsets' true, 'returns the original assignment when the pointer names...' vacuously true, 'refusing otherwise' true. It PASSES. The amended T0 mutation row at SPEC.md:533 does not reach it either -- it names 'assigns fresh offsets to a retry' and 'keyed on the bare (podId, flushSeq)', and blanket refusal is neither. The result is that the ambiguous-PUT retry, which is the ONLY reason M4.10 exists (Sequencer.java:46: 'a retry is safe only once the sequencer ignores a replay of a (podId, flushSeq) it has already applied'), returns an error instead of its offsets, the producer's records are stranded, and the checkpoint pays the pointer's two longs per pod for a field nothing ever consults. That is precisely the 'record it, checkpoint it, recover it, never consult it' no-op that baselines/review.txt records as the round-5 finding against M4.10's own prescriptions, reintroduced one document over. The row's stated property number one -- 'A replay must be ANSWERED, not merely detected' -- now has no criterion that fails without it.
findings.surviving_mutation: In M4.10d, leave `CheckpointWriter`'s new pointer field at its zero/sentinel value on every merge (write the watermark, never the (epoch, sequence)), and make the replay branch always return the distinguishable refusal. Amended criterion 6 and the amended T0 row at SPEC.md:533 both pass.
findings.suggested_fix: One clause: require the pointer to be RECORDED for every applied commit, so that a replay of the pod's most recent flushSeq -- the case the pointer is guaranteed to cover, and the ambiguous-PUT retry the seam exists for -- is always ANSWERED and never refused. The 'refuse rather than return another flush's offsets' bound then applies only to a replay BELOW the pointed flushSeq, which is what ADR-0036's Consequences actually argues.

findings.title: The PARTIAL hoist -- the one mutation the ADR names as uncaught -- survives the fixture requirement and the assertion the ADR prescribes to catch it, and the notes' recommended remedy fixture has the same uniform-flushSeq defect the notes just disqualified the two-pod case for
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0036:121 requires the per-segment triple be asserted 'on a fixture whose triple varies in at least one field per segment', then at :123 names the PARTIAL hoist -- podId per segment, incarnation and flushSeq once per delta -- as 'the mutation none of the three catches today ... because BatchingSequencerTest asserts only hasSize(2)', which reads as: add the per-segment assertion and it dies. It does not. 'Varies in at least one field' is satisfied by podId alone, and the partial hoist KEEPS podId per segment. I measured the two fixtures the notes point at. (1) BatchedCommitDeltaTest's `batched()` (format/src/test/java/binjava/format/BatchedCommitDeltaTest.java:41-46) is three segments differing only in key string; give them a shared incarnation and a shared flushSeq -- the minimum that satisfies the ADR -- and under encode-once-fan-out-on-decode the hoisted incarnation and flushSeq fan back out to the identical values, so `isEqualTo(original)` at :54 and any per-segment triple read both PASS. (2) The notes at :273-276 disqualify BatchingSequencerTest's two-pod `commitAll` partly BECAUSE `from("pod0", 0)` / `from("pod1", 0)` carry 'identical flushSeq', then recommend the three-pod fixture as 'the strongest per-segment fixture available and the natural place to add the triple assertion' -- but that fixture is `new CommitRequest("pod" + pod, 0, ...)` at sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/BatchingSequencerTest.java:152-153, flushSeq literal 0 for all three pods, the SAME defect. (3) The new discriminating golden does not close it either, for the reason this ADR already accepts about goldens: it is generated from whatever encoder the M4.10c author writes, so a partial-hoist encoder produces a self-consistent golden that passes. The consequence is the M5 harm the ADR spends a paragraph on and baselines/review.txt records as its round-2 finding: incarnation and flushSeq carried once per delta drop every pod but one on the first forwarded multi-pod batch, and M4.10d then compares a pod's replay against a FOREIGN pod's watermark -- accepting a real replay or suppressing a real commit, with M4.10c green.
findings.surviving_mutation: In M4.10c, encode `podId` per SegmentCommit but write `incarnationId` and `flushSeq` once for the whole delta, fanning the single pair out to every segment on decode. BatchedCommitDeltaTest's whole-record `isEqualTo(original)`, a per-segment triple read-back on that fixture, the same read-back on BatchingSequencerTest's three-pod delta, and a freshly generated discriminating golden all pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the field, not a quantifier: the fixture carrying the per-segment assertion must vary `flushSeq` (or `incarnationId`) BETWEEN SEGMENTS OF ONE DELTA, not only `podId` -- e.g. two requests from the SAME pod at flushSeq 0 and 1 in one batch, which `CommitLog.commitAll`'s distinct-key rule already permits since their segment keys differ. Alternatively delete the causal clause 'because BatchingSequencerTest asserts only hasSize(2)' at ADR-0036:124, which is what makes the prescription read as sufficient when it is not.
